title: SpMV, load balance, and BFS
brief: Build CSR from COO, price COO, CSR, ELL, and hybrid storage, split SpMV by merge path, measure the load imbalance of three SpMV schemes, and run frontier and direction-optimizing BFS in plain Python. Three CUDA SpMV kernels run on a GPU and are checked against torch.sparse.
hints: Start with coo_to_csr. Sum duplicate (row, column) pairs, sort by row and then column, count the entries of each row, and take a running sum. row_ptr has n_rows + 1 entries, and row i owns the half-open range row_ptr[i] to row_ptr[i + 1].
In spmv_csr the loop is range(row_ptr[i], row_ptr[i + 1]). Stopping at row_ptr[i + 1] - 1 drops the last entry of every row, and a row with one entry returns 0.

ELL stores n_rows * width entries, and width is the longest row. The Bell and Garland hybrid rule adds a column to the ELL part while at least one third of the rows reach that column. The entries past that width go to COO.

Merge path merges two lists: the row end offsets row_ptr[1:] and the nonzero indices 0, 1, 2, and so on. A worker's share is an equal number of steps, rows plus nonzeros. Binary search the row count on a diagonal: row mid is behind the diagonal when row_ptr[mid + 1] <= diagonal - 1 - mid.
Splitting by rows alone, or by nonzeros alone, leaves one worker with the longest row. The merge-path partition has to equal a brute-force walk of the path at every boundary.

warp_work counts iterations in a lockstep model. A warp of 32 lanes on 32 rows runs as long as its longest row. A warp on one row runs ceil(length / 32) iterations. A merge-path warp runs ceil(share / 32).

bottom_up_step accepts a parent only when its level equals the current depth, and it labels the new vertices after the scan. Labeling a vertex at once and accepting any labeled neighbor lets a chain of vertices join one round, and the levels come out too small.
The CUDA part compiles with nvcc on the first run, which takes 30 to 60 seconds. On a machine without a GPU it is skipped, and the CPU checks still run.
